security.evidence: Cors.php:37 accepts any origin with an allowed prefix (`stripos($origin, $pattern) === 0` matches `http://localhost.attacker.com`) and routes/api.php:9-11 echoes an arbitrary Origin; TotemApiController.php:17-20 never compares `{entity}` with the token's entity (no 403), and TotemAuth.php:31-38 never checks that the preset belongs to the claim/totem entity; scope ignores the JWT `queues` claim (TotemApiController.php:21,51,75) so newly attached preset queues are usable by old tokens; the non-locked consume/create sequence permits two totems from one code.

issues.explanation: `public function active(): ` has a colon with no return type, so the file is a PHP parse error and the model — and therefore pairing, auth and both controllers — cannot be loaded.

Both Kernel classes and routes/api.php are new files and nothing wires them up (no bootstrap/app.php change); in the Laravel skeleton this project uses (evidenced by `#[Fillable]`) those Kernel files are dead, so the `cors`/`totem.auth` aliases never register and the api routes are never loaded; the Console Kernel additionally type-hints the non-existent `Illuminate\Foundation\Inspiring\Schedule` and would drop all global middleware via `$middleware = []` if it were used.

`{entity}` is never compared with the token's entity and the preset/totem/claim entity agreement is never checked, so a token can address another entity's paths (and any queue id present in its preset joins) instead of getting `403 {"code":"forbidden"}`.

The effective scope ignores the JWT `queues` claim (`jwt_queues` is stored but never used), so a queue attached to the preset after pairing becomes usable with an old token — the opposite of the required intersection.
No Pest/PHPUnit test ships with the change, although the conventions forbid production code without a test and the task defines a numbered error contract that must be exercised.

Origin matching is a raw prefix check that accepts `http://localhost.attacker.com`/`http://127.0.0.1.evil`, and the preflight route echoes any `Origin` back without validation, so arbitrary sites get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

CORS runs only on the hard-coded `OPTIONS /totem/auth` closure and no other api response gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, while the preflight omits `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`/`-Methods`, so the totem web build cannot make the actual Authorization-bearing calls; `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false` should simply be omitted.
Throttling returns the framework default body instead of `429 {"code":"rate_limited"}`, and the 30/min limiter is applied to the whole group, throttling the read endpoints too.
`{queue:slug}` resolves globally, so another entity's queue is found and handled (403/200) instead of `404 {"code":"queue_not_found"}`; queue lookup must be constrained to the `{entity}`.

The atomic pairing requirement is not met: the preset is looked up outside the transaction, the transaction only saves `login_code_consumed_at` without `lockForUpdate`, and the totem row is created after it, allowing two totems from one code under concurrency.

`visual` is passed through unchanged (no 1-based `order` position in the queue list) and every priority gets `visual: []` instead of `color`/`icon`/`order`, so the documented payload shape is not met.
Only successful pairings are logged; the task requires an audit entry for pairing failures too (and the project logging guidance is not followed for the audit trail).

The task explicitly asks to move the API doc from proposal to implemented contract and update the schema/architecture docs; none of that, nor the CHANGELOG entry required by the conventions, is in the diff.
The backend-owned priority list is copy-pasted three times (endpoint, issuance validation, label lookup) instead of a single source shared by both paths.

`expires_in` and the `exp` claim read a config value that is a string when supplied through `phpunit.xml`, so the response emits `"3600"` rather than the numeric 3600 the contract specifies; `jti` also uses non-cryptographic `uniqid()` (:71).
The pinned test secret `test_secret_32_chars_long_here_` is 31 characters, below the required minimum of 32.
`code` is not checked to be scalar before `preg_match`, so a JSON array/object produces a TypeError and a 500 instead of `400 invalid_code_format`.
Unused imports (`IssueTicket`, `TicketStatus`, `InactiveQueueException`) and a missing `BelongsTo` return type on `Totem::entity()` differ from the sibling models' style.
Overriding `getRouteKeyName()` on the shared `Queue` model changes route binding for every existing queue route, although the totem routes already bind `{queue:slug}` explicitly.

review.summary: The change adds the totem data model, artisan pairing command, pairing endpoint with a hand-rolled HS256 JWT, auth middleware, the three scoped endpoints reusing IssueTicket, CORS handling and config, but it does not work as delivered: TotemPreset.php has a parse error, the new Kernel/routes wiring does not match the framework skeleton, and there are no tests or docs updates. The authorization/scope model is incomplete (no entity check, JWT `queues` claim ignored, global queue binding), the pairing transaction is not locked, and the CORS middleware's prefix matching accepts arbitrary origins, so the pull request needs substantial rework before it can be approved.
